articles.title: Football Daily - Can anyone manage Manchester United? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Rick & Lloyd are joined by Oliver Kay & Joe Smith after a surreal day at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 25 Oct 2026 , · 40 mins

Rick & Lloyd are joined by Oliver Kay, Senior football writer at The Athletic, Joe Smith from Stretford Paddock and BBC Sport’s Chief football news reporter Simon Stone after a surreal day at Old Trafford. Can anyone pull Manchester United out of this mess? Michael Carrick suffered a tumultuous afternoon, where defeat on the pitch came with support in the stands – but at the expense of his players. Was this one of the strangest atmospheres we've ever seen at Man Utd? And is there someone, anyone, that will want to take this impossible job? If not, could Michael Carrick be safe after all... We try to get to the bottom of all of those questions swirling around Old Trafford. Oh, and would a hug from Lloyd make everything better? Rick thinks probably not. Manchester United fans, drop us a WhatsApp on 08000 289 369. TIMECODES 0:00 - Reaction to Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth 3:04 - Do the fans want Michael Carrick to stay? 6:30 - Was leaving Bruno Fernandes on the bench really a ‘football decision’? 9:33 - It looked easy for Bournemouth 11:02 - What do Manchester United need to do now? 15:00 - Have these players got too much baggage? 17:33 - Does Man Utd's 'right' manager exist? 25:20 - Why we felt sorry for Michael Carrick 27:30 - Simon Stone joins the podcast 28:50 - Will Michael Carrick still be in a job by next week? 31:45 - Man Utd’s next five games and a surprising Carrick replacement 34:15 - The Ballon d’Or in London! 36:05 - Can Harry Kane win it?

articles.title: Rinsha Maryam's journey from Bengaluru to Portugal
articles.summary: BENGALURU: After wearing the Bengaluru FC colours in the Super Division during the 2023-24 season, teenager Rinsha Maryam has now joined the Portuguese
articles.body: BENGALURU: After wearing the Bengaluru FC colours in the Super Division during the 2023-24 season, teenager Rinsha Maryam has now joined the Portuguese side Clube de Albergaria U-19 women’s team .On Saturday, the 18-year-old travelled to Lisbon for a round 4 match in the U-19 Liga Feminina against Benfica U-19. She debuted in the club’s season opener against Rio Tinto U-19 last month.The youngster, whose family hails from Kasargod, Kerala, grew up in Bengaluru. “For the last two and a half years, she has been studying and playing in Portugal,”Rinsha’s father Rasheed MP told TOI.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Eterno Oblak
articles.standfirst: El meta esloveno vive un gran inicio de temporada
articles.summary: El meta esloveno vive un gran inicio de temporada
articles.body: Es el futbolista al que más veces han intentado enterrar. Jan Oblak. El portero del Atlético vive un comienzo de curso a la altura de sus mejores versiones. El esloveno volvió a ser decisivo ante el Deportivo, como ya lo había sido frente al Stuttgart, el Espanyol o el United. Suma y sigue. El cancerbero rojiblanco vive una segunda juventud y está plenamente metido en la pelea por el Trofeo Zamora. De lograrlo, dejaría su marca en una cifra prácticamente inalcanzable para cualquier mortal. Conseguir su séptimo galardón como guardameta menos goleado de LaLiga acercaría a los del Cholo a la lucha por el título. Ante el Deportivo volvió a dejar la portería a cero. Fue la quinta vez que lo logra en Liga esta temporada. El 50 % de los partidos disputados por los rojiblancos en la competición doméstica terminaron con el esloveno sin tener que recoger el balón del fondo de su portería. En todos esos encuentros volvió a dejar muestras del portero que sigue siendo. Ante los gallegos sumó cinco paradas, dos de ellas salvadoras. En el primer tiempo, y tras rehacerse de un mal blocaje, un pie milagroso evitó el gol de Amatucci. No fue la única gran intervención de la noche del sábado. En el último suspiro, la fortuna se alió con él para salvar sobre la línea el gol de Kevin. Un milagro en forma de parada para dar los tres puntos al Atlético. Con un coeficiente de 0,80 en la clasificación del Zamora, el esloveno ocupa la segunda posición, por detrás de Radu (0,70), en la pelea por levantar su séptimo trofeo. Oblak ha recibido ocho goles en diez partidos, por los siete del meta del Celta. Unos números que permiten al Atlético vivir su mejor momento de la temporada. De hecho, los rojiblancos tan solo han encajado dos goles en sus últimos seis encuentros ligueros. Durante esta racha, los de Simeone mantuvieron su portería a cero en cuatro de esos seis partidos. Una buena muestra del gran momento que atraviesa Oblak. Tan solo Real Madrid y Alavés han logrado batir al esloveno desde mediados de septiembre. Ante Real Sociedad, Osasuna, Espanyol y Deportivo, el meta echó el cerrojo. Frente a los catalanes protagonizó una parada en el último suspiro para salvar otro triunfo rojiblanco. Igual que ante el Deportivo: un gol a favor y portería a cero. La vieja receta del cholismo. Pero no solo está brillando en LaLiga. Ante Stuttgart y United firmó hasta cuatro paradas de mucho mérito para sostener a los suyos en los momentos más complicados. Resulta curioso cómo, cada vez que alguien pretende enterrar a Oblak, el esloveno vuelve a aparecer para cerrar cualquier debate. De momento, sigue acumulando partidos como rojiblanco (551) hasta situarse a tan solo dos de igualar a Adelardo como el segundo jugador con más encuentros disputados con la camiseta del Atlético. Por delante solo quedará la mayor leyenda del club, Jorge Resurrección, 'Koke', aunque eso son palabras mayores. Un portero irrepetible, de esos que parecen destinados a no volver a encontrarse en la historia rojiblanca. La temporada del Atlético estará marcada, en gran medida, por la de un Oblak eterno.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or Feminin 2026 Power Rankings: Alexia Putellas on course to end Aitana Bonmati's three-year dominance of the Women's Golden Ball
articles.summary: The Barcelona midfielder has won each of the last three prizes - but the 2026 accolade will go to someone else at Monday's ceremony in London after Bonmati's...
articles.body:
The Barcelona midfielder has won each of the last three prizes - but the 2026 accolade will go to someone else at Monday's ceremony in London after Bonmati's injury-hit campaign

Aitana Bonmati has won each of the last three Ballons d'Or Feminin - but the accolade will go to someone else in 2026. Will it be two-time winner and fellow Barcelona star Alexia Putellas who reasserts herself as the best player in the women's game? Or could there be a new name on the honour roll when the Golden Ball is handed out in London on Monday?

Unfortunately, Bonmati suffered a fractured fibula last November, one which required surgery and kept her on the sidelines until she made her return in May. She was still able to play her part as the Catalans won a quadruple, beating Lyon in the Champions League final , but not one big enough to even be nominated for a fourth Ballon d'Or.

Adding to the intrigue is the fact that this was not a World Cup year in women's football, with the Africa Cup of Nations, won by Cameroon back in August , also not counting towards the voting for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Feminin. As such, it is performances for club in the 2025-26 season that will largely decide the ranking for this award, with the exception of those who participated in the Asian Cup, won by Japan , back in March.

So, who are the front-runners for the 2026 award? GOAL runs through the likeliest winners of the Golden Ball ahead of the much-anticipated ceremony...

In 2025-26: 23 clean sheets. Won UEFA Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espanam & Copa de la Reina.

There are some games in which Cata Coll, as the goalkeeper in this dominant Barcelona team, doesn't have much to do. However, that just makes the instances where she is called into action all the more impressive.

This year's Champions League final was a great example of as much . The final scoreline, which read 4-0 to Barca, might suggest that the Catalans had an easy time defeating Lyon to win a fourth European crown, but that is not true. Coll had to be on her A-game in the encounter, making four impressive saves to keep her side ahead before two late Salma Paralluelo goals put the gloss on the final result.

That was one of 23 clean sheets Coll kept during an impressive 2025-26 season for Barca and Spain, in which she helped both teams enjoy fantastic success. Her contributions might sometimes be overlooked, but that Champions League final display should have served as a reminder of their importance and earn her some respect after her first-ever Ballon d'Or nomination.

In 2025-26: Seven goals, five assists. Won UEFA Nations League & FIFA Women's Champions Cup.

After finishing second in the Ballon d'Or voting last year , it's much less likely that Mariona Caldentey will clinch the Golden Ball this time around. The Spain international was certainly influential again for Arsenal, helping them win the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup , but Caldentey's attacking numbers were down on last year, both domestically and in the Champions League, due to the deeper role she was asked to play more consistently at club level.

That is likely to have an impact on her chances, as will the fact that she also struggled to make her mark in the latter stages of the Gunners' European title defence, which was ended by Lyon at the semi-final stage . Expect last year's runner-up to still get votes, though.

In 2025-26: 14 goals, five assists. Won Women's Super League & FA Cup.

An unfortunate spell of injuries mean it's been a while since Vivianne Miedema was last nominated for the Ballon d'Or, with her absent from the final list since finishing 11th in 2022. But the Dutchwoman is widely regarded as one of the best players on the planet and, last season, she reminded everyone just why she recorded back-to-back top-five finishes in the Ballon d'Or voting in the two awards that preceded 2022, by playing a key role in a campaign that delivered Manchester City's first Women's Super League title in 10 years .

Only two players scored more goals in the English top-flight last season than Miedema, who also ranked third for assists and second for combined direct goal contributions. City's lack of European football will hurt her case for matching some of the higher-ranked finishes she's had in the Ballon d'Or before, but the forward still earned herself a nomination after her first injury-free season for a while, with her goal-scoring return in the FA Cup final only enhancing her chances.

In 2025-26: 32 goals, nine assists. Won UEFA Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina.

Claudia Pina had a brilliant 2025-26 season. She won the Golden Boot in Liga F and was one of the most prolific forwards on the continent all season, to the benefit of both Spain, whom she helped win the Nations League, and Barca, who won the quadruple.

However, she endured a little dip in that productivity during the second half of the season, failing to take advantage of the games on the big stage that Barca had. No goals, no assists and no headline-grabbing moments in the Champions League knockout stages, nor in the the Liga F Clasico with Real Madrid, means she sits lower down this ranking - though she did score in the Copa de la Reina final.

In 2025-26: 18 goals, four assists. Won NWSL Shield & Golden Boot.

It's always difficult to know how NWSL stars will be regarded in the Ballon d'Or voting as the league's schedule does not align with the award's parameters in terms of dates and cut-off points. Last year, there were just three NWSL stars nominated, and the presence of both Marta and Esther Gonzalez was more down to their major tournament exploits at international level.

Temwa Chawinga's nomination, however, was rooted in her outstanding NWSL form. In the 2024 season, for which the final few months were relevant for the Ballon d'Or, Chawinga won the Golden Boot and Most Valuable Player awards. In the 2025 season, she once again collected both accolades while also helping the Kansas City Current win the NWSL Shield, and she's been electric in the 2026 campaign, too. As such, the forward should be respected again in the Ballon d'Or ranking, even if her incredible exploits for Malawi on their Women's Africa Cup of Nations debut do not fall into the period considered for voting.

In 2025-26: Six goals, five assists. Won Asian Cup, Women's Super League & FA Cup.

Nominated in 2023 and 2024, Yui Hasegawa is on the longlist again in 2026 after she was the heartbeat of a Man City team which took the WSL by storm last season. Playing in a brilliant double-pivot midfield with England youngster Laura Blindkilde Brown or United States international Sam Coffey, Hasegawa was given more license to get forward, which resulted in more goal contributions that will only aid her cause.

That Hasegawa was a key player in Japan's Asian Cup triumph adds to her credentials in a big way, putting another trophy on her resumé alongside the WSL title that City claimed rather comfortably and the FA Cup triumph that came via a 4-0 win over Brighton .

In 2025-26: 10 goals, 22 assists. Won Bundesliga, DFB-Supercup & DFB-Pokal.

Players in Germany can be overlooked in the voting for this award, but Klara Buhl's incredible numbers cut through in 2025 and did so again in 2026 after another excellent season.

The flying winger matched her goals and surpassed her assists in the Bundesliga from the 2024-25 campaign, with her Champions League numbers also soaring thanks to a remarkable eight assists in her first six games. Those numbers came despite Buhl missing two months with a muscle injury, with her playing a major role in Bayern clinching another domestic treble to put herself back among the Ballon d'Or nominees.

In 2025-26: 29 goals, 10 assists. Won FIFA Women's Champions Cup.

Last year, Alessia Russo finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting. In 2025-26, on an individual basis, she had an even better season; however, it must be said that the role Russo played in England's successful European title defence and Arsenal's Champions League triumph both contributed to her lofty finish in the 2025 voting. As such, the Gunners' semi-final exit from the latter and their inability to pick up any other major trophy, bar the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup, will hamper the striker's 2026 Ballon d'Or bid.

That said, Russo's numbers last season were excellent and they helped Arsenal enjoy what was still a great Champions League run, with her scoring in both knockout ties. She will get well-deserved votes, just probably not as many as last year.

In 2025-26: 18 goals, 16 assists. Won Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina.

There are several factors at play when it comes to the Ballon d'Or Feminin. Of course, the performances and statistics of each individual are a major one, especially on the biggest stages, as is winning silverware. But it would be naive not to note the importance of name recognition when it comes to this award, too. There have been many strange omissions over the years, though few were as glaring as Barcelona maestro Caroline Graham Hansen, who had to wait until 2024 for her first nomination.

The Norway international has, thankfully, finally broken through that glass ceiling now and is in the mix again in 2026. Only one player had more direct goal involvements in Liga F last season than Graham Hansen, who led the division for assists, and the Barca star regularly rose to the occasion too, with some fantastic performances in the Champions League knockout stages.

In 2025-26: Four goals, 10 assists. Won Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina.

After missing over two months due to a broken bone in her foot, forcing her to watch from afar as Spain won the Nations League, Patri Guijarro came back with a bang in 2026. Her importance at Barcelona was evident as soon as she returned, with the team's level rising to a degree that her time on the sidelines has not prevented her from receiving another inclusion on the Ballon d'Or longlist.

Previously finishing as high as sixth in the voting for this award, Guijarro could get near that again in 2026 after a strong end to the season which included a fantastic performance in the Champions League final, with her assist for Ewa Pajor's second goal a stand-out moment .

In 2025-26: 34 goals, 14 assists. Won Bundesliga, DFB-Supercup & DFB-Pokal.

After ranking second in the first-ever Ballon d'Or Feminin vote back in 2018, Pernille Harder is still going incredibly strong in 2026. The Denmark international likely would have a Golden Ball on her mantlepiece had the accolade been dished out in 2020, and she remains highly thought of by voters, ranking 20th last year despite her Denmark side crashing out in the group stages of Euro 2025 without a point to their name .

That was off the back of a terrific treble-winning campaign with Bayern Munich, and the Bavarians enjoyed the same success in 2025-26, all while Harder produced numbers that eclipsed those of the previous year. Throw in the starring role she played in Bayern's Champions League quarter-final triumph over Manchester United , how impressively she performed despite the semi-final defeat to Barcelona and how she helped an understandably unfancied Denmark qualify automatically for next summer's World Cup , and Harder could be on for her best ranking in the Ballon d'Or for several years.

In 2025-26: 39 goals, nine assists. Won Women's Super League & FA Cup.

While her case for the Golden Ball will likely be limited by a lack of European football, Khadija Shaw should rack up plenty of Ballon d'Or votes later this year because of a fantastic season in front of goal that propelled Man City to a first WSL title in 10 years . Shaw netted 21 goals in 22 league games last term, eight more than anyone else in the division, and also added four assists to make her the most productive player in the WSL by some distance.

The striker than enjoyed further success in the FA Cup, both individually and with her team. A two-goal performance against Chelsea in the semi-finals fired City to Wembley, and Shaw was then outstanding in the final, scoring one and assisting another in the 4-0 win over Brighton .

In 2025-26: 22 goals, 12 assists. Won Premiere Ligue, Coupe de la Ligue & Coupe de France.

It'd be a huge surprise if Melchie Dumornay doesn't win the Ballon d'Or at some point, she is just that good. It's a point she proved time and time again with her performances for Lyon last season, as she regularly stood out as the best player on the pitch.

After scoring at a remarkable rate in the 2024-25 season, Dumornay assisted more regularly last term, but she still found the back of the net in big moments - and in spectacular fashion. That was the case when Lyon met PSG in the Coupe de la Ligue final, as her wonderful hit proved to be the only goal in the game, and she opened the scoring in the Coupe de France final too, before netting a hat-trick in the league title-decider as OL completed a domestic treble.

In the Champions League, Dumornay was also decisive to help her side reach the final. On the scoresheet in the quarter-final win over Wolfsburg and named Player of the Match as OL knocked out Arsenal in the last four, these are the sort of performances that should see her rank well.

In 2025-26: 33 goals, seven assists. Won Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina.

Ewa Pajor's role in Barcelona's quadruple-winning 2025-26 campaign should put her right near the top of the Ballon d'Or voting, if not at the top. In 2025, the Poland international collected the Gerd Muller Trophy for her goal-scoring exploits and also ranked eighth in the voting for the main award. As a genuine contender to claim the Golden Ball, she should place even higher this term.

Pajor may not have broken the 50-goal barrier that she managed in 2024-25, but she was still extremely prolific and turned up in huge games, netting in all five of Barca's Champions League knockout matches as they saw off Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and then beat Lyon in the final. Her two goals in that showpiece event were decisive, as she won the title for the first time in her sixth final .

In 2025-26: 24 goals, 13 assists. Won UEFA Women's Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina.

For many, Alexia Putellas would have been a deserving winner of the 2025 Ballon d'Or Feminin. The Barcelona icon arguably looked better than ever during the 2024-25 season, putting some tough years of injury behind her to produce an other-worldly level as the Catalans won a domestic treble and reached the Champions League final.

Putellas carried that form into the 2025-26 season, where the weight of expectation was on her shoulders even more at times amid injuries in midfield to Guijarro and Bonmati. The two-time Ballon d'Or winner excelled in helping younger players around her step up to fill the absences of big names, while still producing a very impressive return of goals and assists that helped both Spain and Barca win everything possible.

Given her consistently world-class level, the track record she has in the Golden Ball voting and the role she played in Barca winning a quadruple, plus early award recognition like the Champions League Player of the Season accolade, Putellas is the front-runner for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Feminin.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho SLAMS 'sleeping' VAR after Real Madrid's dramatic Clasico triumph
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho could not resist criticising the match officials after Real Madrid secured a vital victory against Barcelona. The Portuguese tactician aimed hi...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho could not resist criticising the match officials after Real Madrid secured a vital victory against Barcelona. The Portuguese tactician aimed his frustration at the video assistant referee for missing a potential red card during the second half of the Clasico encounter.

Mourinho voiced his frustration with the match officials following his side's crucial 2-1 victory over Barcelona . The Portuguese boss felt a pivotal refereeing decision went against his team during the latest highly-anticipated edition of El Clasico.

The Sunday showdown marked the 10th matchday of a gruelling Liga campaign. Los Blancos ultimately claimed all three points in a fiercely contested battle between the bitter rivals. However, the positive result was slightly overshadowed by Mourinho's explosive post-match comments. He singled out a specific second-half incident involving Barcelona defender Joao Cancelo and Madrid's Yan Diomande.

Mourinho firmly believes Cancelo should have been dismissed in the 60th minute. He argued that the Portuguese full-back committed a dangerous tackle on Diomande that warranted a straight red card. While he praised the on-field referee, Mourinho directed his anger entirely at the video assistants. He accused the technology team of completely missing a clear and obvious error.

"We played a great match against a great opponent," Mourinho stated during his press conference. "With a referee who, in my opinion, had an excellent match, and a VAR that, in my opinion, was sleeping in the 60th minute, because it was clearly a red card for Cancelo's foul on Diomande."

Despite his obvious frustration regarding the VAR intervention, Mourinho ensured he highlighted his team's overall performance. Beating their fierce rivals provided a significant boost to their Liga ambitions. The former Inter Milan coach acknowledged the quality of the opposition on the day. He made sure to praise his players for overcoming the stiff challenge presented by Barcelona.

"But it was a superb match, a superb victory," Mourinho concluded.

Madrid will now look to build on the valuable momentum gained from this crucial Clasico triumph. Securing maximum points against Barcelona keeps Mourinho's men firmly in the hunt for the league title at this early stage of the campaign. Mourinho's side will next travel to face Racing Santander in Liga this weekend.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Who are the leading contenders?
articles.summary: The Ballon d'Or race is rarely decided by numbers alone. Club silverware, individual brilliance and performances on the international stage can all shape the...
articles.body:
The Ballon d'Or race is rarely decided by numbers alone. Club silverware, individual brilliance and performances on the international stage can all shape the vote, with the balance between them often proving decisive.

The 2026 race has produced a fascinating collection of contenders. Harry Kane has enjoyed a prolific season at Bayern Munich , Kylian Mbappé has continued to rewrite goalscoring records, and Lionel Messi has shown he remains capable of delivering on the biggest stage. Meanwhile, Rodri , Lamine Yamal and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia all have compelling cases of their own.

But with major trophies won and individual records broken, who has done enough to claim football's most prestigious individual honour on Monday night?

Team trophies: FA Cup, League Cup, FIFA World Cup.

Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Ball

Rodri knows what it takes to win the Ballon d'Or, having claimed the award in 2024 after an outstanding season for Manchester City and Spain. Another World Cup triumph has strengthened his case for a second victory.

The Spain captain was named Player of the Tournament as La Roja lifted the trophy, recognition of his influence on the biggest stage.

His biggest obstacle is the club campaign. While the World Cup Golden Ball is a major point in his favour, a less successful season at club level leaves him with ground to make up on rivals who combined individual brilliance with domestic and European silverware.

Team trophies: Ligue 1, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup

Individual awards: UEFA Champions League Player of the Season

The Georgian was in devastating form as Paris Saint-Germain made it back-to-back Champions League wins in 2025/26.

Kvaratskhelia scored 10 goals and created six more in 16 European appearances for the Champions League winners, and added nine more goals across all competitions.

Georgia's absence from the World Cup hurts his chances, with major tournaments often decisive in Ballon d'Or votes.

Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Silver Ball, FIFA World Cup Silver Boot, MLS Golden Boot, MLS Most Valuable Player

A record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or looked a real possibility for Lionel Messi as Argentina reached a second straight World Cup final, but defeat to Spain has reduced his chances.

The Ballon d'Or race is crowded with players who have enjoyed exceptional seasons in Europe. Messi's achievements are remarkable, but the strength of the opposition means another victory would require a particularly persuasive argument.

Messi, however, was magnificent in North America, showing that even at 39 he remains one of the game's greatest talents.

Individual awards: FIFA World Cup Golden Boot, FIFA World Cup Bronze Ball, UEFA Champions League Top Scorer, Pichichi Trophy

Kylian Mbappe has argued the Ballon d'Or is an individual accolade that shouldn't be decided by team success. Real Madrid and France both fell short in the big tournaments, despite Mbappe's brilliance.

The leading scorer in La Liga, the Champions League, and World Cup, Mbappe made his mark on the major events. His 10-goal World Cup campaign saw him shatter the all-time goal record and become the first multi-Golden Boot winner.

The absence of major team trophies is the obvious drawback. Ballon d'Or voters have often favoured players who combine individual excellence with collective success, and Mbappé cannot point to a Champions League or World Cup winner's medal this time.

But if the award is genuinely about the best individual player of the year, Mbappé has an argument few can match.

Team trophies: La Liga, Supercopa de España, FIFA World Cup

Individual awards: La Liga Player of the Season, Zarra trophy

Lamine Yamal seems destined for Ballon d'Or success at some stage, after a runners-up finish last year. At 19, he would become the youngest-ever winner, following a sensational season that delivered La Liga and World Cup success.

He scored 16 goals and assisted 11 more during Barcelona 's title win, but failed to have a major impact - despite success - for Spain in the summer. He scored just once in eight games during an injury-impacted World Cup.

Team trophies: Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, German Super Cup

Individual awards: Bundesliga top scorer, European Golden Shoe

Harry Kane might have the most well-rounded argument of any contender.

The Bayern Munich striker scored 61 goals in 51 games as his side secured a domestic treble, while his scoring record earned him the European Golden Shoe. Few players can match that combination of individual production and team success.

While England failed to end their tournament drought, Kane's six goals helped the Three Lions to a third-place finish at the World Cup. It represents England's best-ever performance on foreign soil.

Individual awards: Bundesliga Player of the Season

Olise outperformed club teammate Kane to win the Bundesliga's Player of the Season award. The winger scored 15 league goals and provided 19 assists, while he was named in the Team of the Tournament for the Bundesliga, Champions League, and FIFA World Cup.

Olise has the numbers to enter the conversation, but he may need a stronger individual narrative to turn an excellent season into a Ballon d'Or-winning one.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 Live Streaming: How to watch it for free in India
articles.summary: Football fans around the world are gearing up for the Ballon d’Or 2026 awards ceremony, one of the biggest events on the international football calendar.
articles.body: Football fans around the world are gearing up for the Ballon d’Or 2026 awards ceremony, one of the biggest events on the international football calendar.The prestigious awards return for their 70th edition, celebrating outstanding performances by the best players in men’s and women’s football.The ceremony will bring together some of the biggest names in the sport, with several leading stars competing for individual honours.Indian fans looking to follow the action can find details about the Ballon d’Or 2026 date, venue, India timings, live streaming options and complete list of nominees below.Ballon d’Or 2026: Date and venueThe 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or ceremony is scheduled to take place on Monday, October 26, 2026. The event will be hosted at the London Palladium in London, England.The annual ceremony recognises exceptional performances across men’s and women’s football, with awards presented to players and other influential figures in the game.Ballon d’Or 2026 timings in IndiaFor viewers in India, the main Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony is scheduled to begin at 1:30 AM IST on Tuesday, October 27.The red-carpet coverage is expected to start at 10:30 PM IST on Monday, October 26, giving fans an opportunity to follow the arrivals and pre-ceremony proceedings before the main event begins.Here are the key timings for Indian viewers:Date of ceremony: Monday, October 26, 2026Red-carpet coverage: 10:30 PM IST, October 26Main ceremony: 1:30 AM IST, October 27Venue: London Palladium, London, EnglandHow to watch Ballon d’Or 2026 live streaming in India?Football enthusiasts in India can look for the Ballon d’Or 2026 live stream on DAZN, which has announced free global coverage across 200 markets.Fans planning to watch the awards online should check DAZN’s official platform for the event stream, regional availability and any viewing requirements before the ceremony begins.The online broadcast is expected to offer viewers an opportunity to follow the event, including the presentation of the major individual awards.Ballon d’Or 2026 Live Telecast: Where to Watch on TV in India?As of the information available for this article, an India-specific television broadcaster has not been confirmed for the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony.Viewers who prefer watching the awards on television should check official broadcaster announcements closer to the event. articles.title: Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Mbappé brace wins El Clásico for Los Blacos
articles.summary: Real Madrid won the season’s first El Clásico on Sunday night, thanks to a brace from Kylian Mbappé.The Frenchman put Real ahead shortly before half-time, bu...
articles.body:
Real Madrid won the season's first El Clásico on Sunday night, thanks to a brace from Kylian Mbappé.

The Frenchman put Real ahead shortly before half-time, but Raphinha levelled for Barça on the hour mark.

The match looked to be heading for a draw until Mbappé netted a late winner, causing José Mourinho to kneeslide on the touchline.

Hans-Dieter Flick made two changes to his Barcelona side after their 4-2 loss to PSG on Tuesday night, with Rodri and Fermín López replacing Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal in midfield. Meanwhile, José Mourinho named four changes, with Andriy Lunin, Ibrahima Konaté, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande replacing Thibaut Courtois, Antonio Rüdiger, Álvaro Carreras and Vinicius Junior.

Barcelona dominated large parts of the first half, with Anthony Gordon forcing three saves out of Lunin, and plenty of other chances going begging for the hosts.

The opener came in the 41st minute, when Mbappé arguably got incredibly lucky. It was Diomande's delivery into the box that initially seemed to be dealt with by Gerard Martín; however, the Barça defender could only clear it into the leg of the onrushing striker, who saw the ball bounce into the back of the net off his shin.

Diomande came close himself minutes later, breaking in behind the Barcelona defence before firing his shot into the side netting, meaning the score stayed at 1-0 going into the break.

The first real chance of the second half saw Raphinha draw the hosts level when his left-footed strike from inside the area found its way past Lunin after a clever disguised pass from Pedri.

Arda Güler looked to put Madrid back ahead mere moments later, but Joan García was on hand to palm his shot away from danger. Lunin made a spectacular save in the 65th minute, when he managed to react quickly and keep out Martín's close-range header.

The winning goal came in the 87th minute, when Los Blancos broke away down the left following some superb skill from Jude Bellingham in the middle of the park. The Englishman laid it off to Eduardo Camavinga, who played a nice one-two with Cucurella before setting up Mbappé to tap home from close range and earn Mourinho's side all three points at the Nou Camp.

articles.title: Florian Wirtz brushes off Jamie Carragher's brutal criticism after starring in Liverpool victory
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz has issued a defiant response to the mounting criticism surrounding his performances since joining Liverpool for a club-re...
articles.body:
Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz has issued a defiant response to the mounting criticism surrounding his performances since joining Liverpool for a club-record fee. The German international, who has struggled to maintain consistency, insists he remains focused on his game despite high-profile pundits questioning his output.

The Germany international has found himself under the microscope ever since the Reds committed to a staggering £116.5 million deal to lure him away from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. Despite the pressure of his price tag, the 23-year-old is adamant that he is not listening to the critics who have questioned his output during his time in the Premier League. Wirtz played a pivotal role in the breakthrough against Brighton , as it was his powerful effort that deflected off Pascal Gross to open the scoring. Following that opener, Bradley Barcola provided the assist for Alexander Isak to secure the result.

"Maybe I'm just an interesting guy, you know?" Wirtz joked during a post-match interview with the BBC . The midfielder, who struggled to find consistent rhythm during his debut year under Arne Slot, appears to be enjoying a new lease of life in the current setup. Wirtz currently boasts a tally of one goal and three assists for the current campaign, figures that he will be looking to improve as he seeks to silence his detractors permanently. "No, I just play my football, and if people want to talk about me or judge me, that's their job. I am not focusing on that. I just want to play football, and more, I cannot do," the playmaker added as he continues to adapt to the rigours of English football.

The midfielder hails dominant first-half display

Wirtz then praised his team's mindset and commanding start, highlighting their sharp execution in the opening phase of the game. He noted that throughout the first half—particularly during the initial thirty minutes—the squad asserted control by dominating individual duels, generating numerous scoring opportunities, and pairing their attacking tempo with disciplined defending to close out the half securely.

"We had the right mentality today to go into this game. In the first half or first 30 minutes, we were on top of them and really good in the duels, creating a lot of chances. It's good to end the half and we defended good. Really happy about that," he explained.

"It's really enjoyable. I think many things weren't so good in the last month so I'm even happier that it's going well at the moment. We are in a good way to get where we want to be. We should keep going like that and I'm happy about that."

The most vocal critic of the German star has been Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher, who has repeatedly questioned whether the club received fair value for their money . Following a disappointing loss to Manchester City earlier in the season, Carragher was particularly scathing about the midfielder's contributions to the team. The former defender suggested that Wirtz has had more than enough time to adapt to life in the Premier League.

"There is no way Wirtz should be playing ahead of Gravenberch. What Florian Wirtz is doing for Liverpool is not enough right now. He's played 55, 60 games for Liverpool. He shouldn't be in the Liverpool team right now. I don't want to hammer Liverpool players. But we're not saying this after five-ten games, we're saying this after 50-60 games," Carragher said.

The victory over Brighton was slightly dampened when Wirtz was forced to leave the field prematurely. After receiving medical attention on the pitch, the midfielder was substituted in the 65th minute, causing immediate concern among the Anfield faithful. The German was eventually replaced by Trey Nyoni as the medical staff began their initial checks on the sidelines during the closing stages of the match.

Head coach Andoni Iraola was quick to provide an update on the situation, though he admitted that the congested fixture schedule makes any fitness issue a potential problem. "Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle. It doesn't look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is," Iraola noted.

articles.title: Hansi Flick identifies Barcelona’s biggest problem after Real Madrid defeat: ‘We weren’t fresh’
articles.summary: Hansi Flick has admitted Barcelona were not physically fresh enough after suffering a 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season...
articles.body:
Hansi Flick has admitted Barcelona were not physically fresh enough after suffering a 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season.

The Barcelona manager refused to make excuses after his side lost at home, but acknowledged that fatigue, defensive injuries and a demanding schedule have affected the team's performances.

The defeat was Barcelona's first in 10 La Liga matches and their second loss in the same week.

Flick has now challenged his players to recover quickly, improve their energy levels and respond before the international break, while also considering further opportunities for La Masia prospects amid growing defensive concerns.

Flick admits Barcelona lacked freshness against Real Madrid

Flick was disappointed with Barcelona's performance and acknowledged that Real Madrid had improved compared with previous meetings between the rivals.

"We played against an opponent that was better than in previous Clásicos. We weren't fresh. We have to recover, concentrate, and react.

Flick admits Barcelona were not fresh. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"It's not easy, but we have to accept it. Barça has to keep going."

The German manager also explained that Barcelona need to recover the physical sharpness they displayed earlier in the campaign.

"Well, we have to try to switch off and forget about training. We need to regain the freshness we had in the previous matches of the season."

Flick felt Barcelona had performed better after the interval and had managed to restore parity, but their attacking commitment ultimately left them exposed to Madrid's decisive counter-attack.

"I'm not satisfied. Today it was clear we weren't 100% fresh. Normally we would have been fresher. We played well in the second half, and Madrid only had two chances to score a second goal.

"We controlled the game and scored to make it 1-1. In the end, we pressed high, and they countered and scored.

"It's not good for us, but we have to accept it. Defeats are also part of football," Flick said.

The result has increased the pressure on Barcelona to respond, although Flick insisted that one defeat should not define the team's campaign.

"It's our first defeat in ten league matches. We're not playing at our best, and it's related to freshness.

"We have a week to prepare for the next match. We need to get the team's energy back."

Flick refuses to make excuses after two defeats

Barcelona's recent results have raised questions about their ability to deliver in major matches.

Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the La Liga season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Flick acknowledged the concerns and said the team needed to discuss what had gone wrong rather than look for explanations outside its control.

"There are no arguments, no excuses – it's clear. We need to talk. I'm not worried about it in general because, as I said before, it's part of the sport.

"We've had two defeats this week and that's too many for me, and, no doubt, for the Barça fans as well. But this is part of the sport and we have to bounce back."

The manager also addressed the demanding travel schedule after Barcelona's trip to Seville, although he was reluctant to use it to explain the Clasico loss.

Several players are due to attend the Ballon d'Or Gala in London before returning to training.

"In Seville, we spent three hours on the plane, then we stayed there to sleep. But I don't want to talk about that now if we've lost.

"Perhaps I'll do so when we win, because it might sound like an excuse. Now many players will be going to London for the Ballon d'Or Gala, and they'll be back. We'll rest on Tuesday and get back to work on Wednesday.

"I want to win both matches before the international break – it's important.

"Players like Espart, Olmo and Eric have picked up knocks and are injured. We don't have many more options in defence and we'll have to manage it."

Flick considers La Masia options amid defensive injury concerns

Barcelona's injury problems could force Flick to look towards the club's academy as he attempts to manage the squad through the coming fixtures.

Flick admits Barcelona might have to call up players from the youth team. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images)

With defensive options limited, the manager is hoping some injured players will return soon enough to ease the pressure.

"We may have to call up more players from La Masia. We'll sort it out. We're expecting Christensen and Eric back soon. And we'll see if we have any good news."

Flick also explained why Frenkie de Jong was introduced during the match, pointing to the midfielder's recent training performances and the boost he could provide to the team.

"We've been thinking about where to position him on the pitch. He'd been training well, he was giving us a boost, so we decided to bring him on and give him some playing time," he concluded.

articles.title: Premier League Team of the Week: Our Best XI
articles.summary: The Premier League Team of the Week is headlined by Aston Villa’s statement victory over Manchester City, Tottenham’s impressive triumph at Chelsea and Bourn...
articles.body:
The Premier League Team of the Week is headlined by Aston Villa 's statement victory over Manchester City, Tottenham's impressive triumph at Chelsea and Bournemouth 's latest demolition of Manchester United at Old Trafford.

From Zion Suzuki's outstanding display in goal to Nicolas Jackson 's match-winning double, this week's selection celebrates the players who made the biggest impact across the Premier League , with several summer signings continuing to make their mark.

It's time to give Aston Villa their flowers for their summer rebuild. There were fears when several senior stars were sold in the summer, but Villa look to have recruited brilliantly.

Zion Suzuki has made his presence felt in goal and recorded 1.74 Expected Goals prevented against Manchester City.

Summed up an excellent performance from Aston Villa with a dogged defensive display against Manchester City.

Jeremy Doku is one of the most difficult direct opponents in the Premier League , but Cash gave everything in their one-vs-one battle. Eight tackles emphasised his good work.

James Hill might be one of the most under-appreciated players in the Premier League. Since breaking in as a Bournemouth regular last season, Hill has been immense.

At Manchester United he was superb again, leading the contest for tackles and clearances. A big win for Bournemouth, who have made Old Trafford a playground in recent years.

Arsenal 's aerial threat returned against Everton with centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel on the scoresheet in a 2-0 win at the Emirates.

Gabriel's emphatic header made the result safe, after a performance that saw the big Brazilian dominate his duel with Thierno Barry.

Left-back: Adrien Truffert - Bournemouth

The sort of all-action performance we've come to expect from Adrien Truffert. The left-back punished Leny Yoro's slip to set up Marcus Tavernier's goal, continuing on the form that saw him earn an international call up for France under Zinedine Zidane.

Central midfield: Nico Gonzalez - Newcastle

Looked a class above as Newcastle earned an important three points at Crystal Palace. The Spaniard snapped into tackles, picking up a booking in the process, but dealt with that setback with trademark cool. Came out on top in his duel with Adam Wharton.

Central midfield: Mateus Fernandes - Tottenham

The sort of performance that begins to justify Spurs' big summer spend. Fernandes was everywhere in an outstanding performance at Stamford Bridge, leading the contest for touches, passes, successful tackles and dribbles.

If any player epitomised how Tottenham are improving, it was Fernandes.

A real menace to the Brighton backline. Barcola forced Liverpool 's second goal after charging down Oliver Boscagli's clearance and powering past the defender to set up Alexander Isak.

The Frenchman was a threat all afternoon and got through plenty of defensive work too.

Left-wing: Mathys Tel - Tottenham Hotspur

One of his best performances in a Spurs shirt. Tel provided a constant outlet for the North Londoners at Chelsea, with his directness and pace stretching the home side.

The Frenchman sealed a memorable win with a brilliant individual goal, charging into space before drilling past Mike Penders.

Centre-forward: Nicolas Jackson - Aston Villa

Reborn at Aston Villa. Jackson's double downed Manchester City to make it six goals in six games. The Senegalese striker was unwanted at Chelsea, but is full of confidence after reuniting with Unai Emery at Villa Park.

There's always been a lot to like about Jackson, but a flurry of recent goals suggest there's more to come.

A thorn in the Manchester United side, Evanilson has started the season with a bang at Bournemouth.

Another tireless performance was rewarded with a superb goal at Old Trafford, as Evanilson rounded Senne Lammens and finished from a difficult angle. That's three goals and four assists in eight games this season for the Brazilian.

articles.title: Chiefs’ Andy Reid delivers reality check for Harrison Butker after kicker’s SNF misses
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs had a Sunday night to forget, dropping a 20-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks in a primetime matchup where virtually nothing went ri...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs had a Sunday night to forget, dropping a 20-3 loss against the Seattle Seahawks in a primetime matchup where virtually nothing went right. While the offense sputtered across four quarters, veteran kicker Harrison Butker endured an uncharacteristically rough outing that left head coach Andy Reid offering a firm reality check after the game.

Butker converted just 1-of-3 field goal attempts on the night, finishing with a meager 33.3% success rate. The three-time Super Bowl champion did manage to drill a 50-yard field goal to put Kansas City on the scoreboard, but his two misfires proved exceptionally costly. The most agonizing pull came early in the fourth quarter on a 45-yard attempt. Trailing 13-3 at the time, a successful kick would have trimmed the deficit down to a single possession. Instead, the ball sailed wide right, deflating Kansas City's sideline before Seattle pulled away late for the comfortable home victory.

Addressing reporters during his postgame press conference, Reid delivered a candid assessment regarding his usually automatic placekicker's recent form.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but he's off a bit — gotta fix it," Reid said.

Reid's honest comments highlight growing concern over Butker's early-season struggles. The Georgia Tech product earned a lucrative contract extension during the offseason that made him one of the highest-paid kickers in the National Football League. For years, Butker has served as Kansas City's ultimate security blanket , routinely delivering clutch postseason heroics and long-range field goals with effortless precision. Seeing him misfire on manageable attempts raises immediate red flags for an elite contender that relies heavily on fine margins.

The Chiefs simply cannot afford to leave free points on the turf as the regular season grind intensifies. Reid still holds full faith in his veteran specialist, but the takeaway remains crystal clear: Butker must recalibrate quickly before those missed kicks start turning tight contests into agonizing losses.

articles.title: Mourinho hails 'extraordinary' Real Madrid after Mbappé double sinks Barcelona in El Clásico
articles.summary: José Mourinho says his Real Madrid players produced an 'extraordinary' performance after Kylian Mbappé's double secured a 2-1 Clásico win over Barcelona at C...
articles.body:
José Mourinho says his Real Madrid players produced an 'extraordinary' performance after Kylian Mbappé's double secured a 2-1 Clásico win over Barcelona at Camp Nou.

Mbappé opened the scoring in the 41st minute when Gerard Martín fired a clearance straight into him, before Raphinha levelled in the 61st minute.

Mbappé then struck the winner in the 87th minute, tucking in Eduardo Camavinga's cutback after sublime skill from Jude Bellingham.

The result ended Barcelona's perfect start to the season. Hansi Flick's side had won all nine of their La Liga fixtures and would have broken Madrid's 1968-69 record for the best ever start in the Spanish top flight with another win.

Jose Mourinho's side had started the game six points behind their fierce rivals and knew defeat would have left them with a long road back in the title race.

Mbappe's double instead sees Madrid move to 24 points from 10 games, three behind La Liga leaders Barcelona and one behind second-placed Atlético Madrid.

The Frenchman's brace also continued a remarkable record in Spain's biggest fixture. Mbappe has now scored eight goals in seven Clásicos, and 14 goals in 11 career games against Barcelona. He also moved to 100 goals in 116 games for Real Madrid.

Mourinho had insisted before the game that the Clásico would not decide whether his side can win things this season.

"A game that the world which loves football stopped to see"

Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised both sides for the spectacle before turning to his own players.

"I think it was a great game," Mourinho said.

"A game at a high level, a game that the world which loves football stopped to see. And they weren't let down, with two teams that played to win.

"In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage, playing an opponent that presses you a lot. For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent.

"This match was one where we could leave trailing by three, six, or nine points. Obviously, if you fall behind by nine, psychologically, it's heavy. If we were behind by six, it would be balanced. Being three points behind is different, and the way we won is also important because you can win with luck and by defending a lot. We won calmly and with full merit."

articles.title: Jose Mourinho talks Silva, Lunin, Camavinga, Cucurella after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid
articles.summary: Last night was one to remember for Real Madrid fans as they saw their team visit the Spotify Camp Nou and get a 1-2 win over their arch-rivals FC Barcelona....
articles.body:
Last night was one to remember for Real Madrid fans as they saw their team visit the Spotify Camp Nou and get a 1-2 win over their arch-rivals FC Barcelona. As was expected, it turned out to be a hard-fought game in which both the teams tried their best to get a result in their favor, but ultimately, the Merengues' quality shone through and they come back to the Spanish capital reducing the deficit at the top of the La Liga table to three points.

As MARCA has reported, Jose Mourinho addressed the press after this enthralling win. Analyzing the match, the Portuguese coach praised his team for giving their all on the pitch:

"It's been a great match, a high-level game. Two teams that play to win, and in our case, the lads put in a great performance. They were organised and courageous against an opponent who presses a lot. We had chances to score a second goal, including that two-against-one situation with Jude and Kylian.

Barça reacted strongly in the second half, but we remained calm and didn't lose our composure. It was a great victory for the lads. The referee had a great game. VAR was asleep in the 60th minute, with a decision that had a major impact on João's clear red-card offence for the foul on Diomande."

The Real Madrid coach highlighted how important this win could be for the league title, and praised several players for their performances in this game:

"It's a match that could leave us three, six or nine points clear. If you come away nine points ahead, that's a significant gap. If it's six, things are more balanced. If it's three, the situation is different. You can win through luck or by spending much of the game defending, but we won comfortably and fully deserved it.

I've only been here a short time with Bernardo, although I know him well. That's one thing; seeing how he can fit into the team is another. I'll never tell you, 'This is my core team', or talk about indispensable players. We have a complete squad. They work hard and are ready to win.

You've asked me two questions, and neither has been about Lunin. If Lunin makes mistakes, I'm sure the second question will be about him. We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of the players complained before the match because he wasn't playing. The players are united.

We've won five matches in a row, and we have another game on Sunday, in a unique run of three consecutive away matches. Valverde played injured for more than 40 minutes. He wanted to keep going within his limits."

While praising Eduardo Camavinga, Mourinho explained how his team got over the offside trap set by Flick's team:

"Eduardo, like everyone else, is a starting-calibre player. They train for that, and then it's the manager who decides. Some managers look at the bench and have no solutions. Flick brought on De Jong, who is a very powerful engine. Bernardo worked hard against Pedri, and the match required us to bring on fresh legs to keep going and launch counter-attacks.

Against Barcelona, it's often difficult to attack the space because you frequently get caught offside. When the runs come from the second line, as Jude and Camavinga did, it's harder for them to deal with."

Although his team won by the barest of margins, the Portuguese coach was happy with the result:

"I think this was our toughest match against an opponent who had won every league game up to this point. We've beaten several teams by four goals, but this was Barça, and our players put in a great performance."

Mourinho highlighted how his team has improved over the last few weeks:

"We've improved a lot in recent matches. I don't want to go back to the Atlético game, but the Betis match was the one in which we missed the most chances. We didn't play terribly. The group is strong internally, with a growing sense of empathy, and the players support one another. It's a great group to work with. A great group is also one that sticks together when things get difficult.

When we return to work, I won't let everyone walk around with their heads in the clouds. If we lose at El Sardinero, today's victory will mean nothing. Madrid play to win titles."

The Real Madrid coach also highlighted Marc Cucurella's incredible performance in this match:

"We have two high-level left-backs, which allows me to manage their workload a little. Carreras played the previous match, allowing Cucu to be fresh for this one. He did a great job. I always say that I only realise how good players are when I see them in front of me. Watching them on television, I miss certain things. When they're ten metres away, I can appreciate their quality.

He's very good (Lamine), extremely difficult to handle and, as well as being talented, he's clever. He tried everything. This was the toughest match Cucu has faced against a player who is really good."

The Portuguese coach was willing to give all the credit for this win to the players:

"We won because of the players. That's the life of a manager, and it's why so many lose their jobs. I'm very happy for them, for all of them. I'm also happy for Asencio, who wanted to come today and has been talking to the players."

Finally, the Real Madrid coach highlighted his midfield option:

"I've learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mentality to play. In midfield, too, having a combination of different talents gives us more than having two players with similar characteristics.

That's why I wouldn't play Bernardo alongside Güler, except perhaps in desperate situations. The same goes for Camavinga and Tchouaméni today; that combination is for specific circumstances. This blend of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when building attacks."

Although he was gracious enough to give all the credit to his players, there is no doubt Jose Mourinho himself deserves a lot of credit for this memorable win. He clearly got the better of a coach as astute as Hansi Flick in this match, while his work in getting the best out of almost all the Real Madrid players and making the team work as a united group also deserve a lot of commendation.

articles.title: Pundit Claims Arsenal Will ‘100 Per Cent’ Sell Gyökeres Next Summer
articles.summary: Former Aston Villa striker Gabriel Agbonlahor has made a bold prediction about Viktor Gyökeres’ Arsenal future, insisting the Gunners will sell the Swedish i...
articles.body:
Former Aston Villa striker Gabriel Agbonlahor has made a bold prediction about Viktor Gyökeres' Arsenal future, insisting the Gunners will sell the Swedish international next summer.

His comments followed Arsenal's comfortable 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday, a match in which Gyökeres provided an assist but once again failed to get himself on the scoresheet.

And Agbonlahor clearly wasn't impressed with what he saw.

Agbonlahor Questions Gyökeres' Arsenal Future

Speaking on talkSPORT , Agbonlahor questioned the striker's mobility.

"Looks like he's like running in slow motion, isn't he?"

He then acknowledged that Gyökeres can hold the ball up, but insisted the 28-year-old would not be at Arsenal next season, confirming:

Agbonlahor went further, suggesting Arsenal would already have moved Gyökeres on if they had managed to secure the signing of Atlético Madrid forward Julián Álvarez.

Of course, this isn't a new idea. Arsenal were repeatedly linked with a Gyökeres-plus-cash deal for Álvarez throughout the summer transfer window, with one report suggesting the Gunners could offer the Swedish striker alongside £68.5 million.

Ultimately, nothing materialised, and Gyökeres remained at Arsenal. But Agbonlahor clearly believes the club will revisit the question of his future next summer.

That's quite a statement about a player who helped Arsenal win the Premier League last season and remains under contract until 2030.

There is no denying that Gyökeres has struggled for goals this season. He managed just 17 touches and failed to register a shot during his 68 minutes against Everton.

For a striker who arrived with such an impressive goalscoring reputation, those numbers are naturally disappointing.

And Saturday was only his first Premier League start of the campaign.

It's certainly fair to question whether Gyökeres is producing enough to justify a regular starting place, particularly with Kai Havertz competing for the same position.

But suggesting Arsenal will definitely sell him next summer seems premature when we're only eight league games into the season.

Arteta has repeatedly spoken positively about the striker, and there is still plenty of football to be played before any decisions about next summer's transfer window need to be made.

Perhaps Agbonlahor will eventually be proved right. But surely Gyökeres deserves more than one league start before his Arsenal future is written off?

articles.title: “Fun way to play football”: Elisabeth Terland reveals how happy Man United Women players are under Eva Olid
articles.summary: Manchester United Women continue their improving performances with a solid 1-1 draw with champions Manchester City.Deserved drawThe Red Devils played well bu...
articles.body:
Manchester United Women continue their improving performances with a solid 1-1 draw with champions Manchester City.

The Red Devils played well but fell behind in the second half.

Nonetheless, this did not deter them, and they forced an equaliser in the 89th minute through Elisabeth Terland.

Her instinctive strike from inside the area was enough to secure a well-deserved draw for Eva Olid's side.

The Norwegian Sky Sports after the game.

The striker echoed her manager's thoughts that the red side could have easily come away with the win.

She explained, "I think, with the way the game evolved, we should be happy with a point. But I'm really happy with the performance today. To be honest, I think we could have gone away with a win. But yeah, we take a point at the end of the day."

Explaining what Eva Olid told them at half-time, she said, "just to go out and do the same, just one step better. I think we had the chances today to get even more goals, even in the first half. We should have been up. I think there's a lot to take from this game, and this is the standard going forward."

Finally, the team have really turned a corner from the start of the season, and Terland was asked about this.

She expressed her joy at being part of this group and feeling the progress.

Terland explained, "it's great. It's a fun way to play football. I think if we can play like this every week, it's something you enjoy so much."

Reflecting on the magnitude of the performance against Manchester City, she added, "I think we're competing against a top team, and we should probably win the game. I think that just speaks for itself. But yeah, it's a good performance."

United will next be in action at home to Burnley in the Players' Cup on Wednesday evening.

articles.title: Jermaine Pennant: Former Premier League winger needs more than 50 stitches after dog attack
articles.summary: Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog.
articles.body:
Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog.

The 43-year-old was walking his two dogs in north London last week when he was attacked by a German Shepherd.

The former Liverpool and Stoke City winger said the dog latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his own dog, King.

King then intervened to help fight off the attacking dog, preventing "what could've been an horrendous situation", Pennant said in a post on Instagram. , external

Pennant told the Sun , external he required more than 50 stitches to his right leg after sustaining four bite wounds in the attack and receiving hospital treatment.

He added that King was unhurt, but did not give details about the German Shepherd. He said he declined to report the attack to police.

"So I was attacked by a German shepherd, I tried to protect King but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until King intervened as he didn't know what was going on," said Pennant.

"But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could've been a horrendous situation for me.

"King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn't mine. At this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn't King's."

The picture uploaded to Instagram shows Pennant with a bandage on his leg alongside King on a sofa, while he also thanked his partner Mimmi Montgomery for looking after them.

"My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me. King you're a legend, love you, man's best friend. Thanks Mimmi Montgomery for taking care of us both."

Pennant, who is a pundit for Talksport, made 231 Premier League appearances in a 19-year career before retiring in 2018.

articles.title: (Video) Two Ronald Araujo moments at Anfield on Sunday show why he’s adored by Liverpool fans
articles.summary: If Liverpool’s win over Villarreal last week was Rio Ngumoha’s night, then the 2-0 victory against Brighton on Sunday was the Ronald Araujo show.The Uruguaya...
articles.body:
If Liverpool's win over Villarreal last week was Rio Ngumoha's night, then the 2-0 victory against Brighton on Sunday was the Ronald Araujo show.

The Uruguayan has swiftly endeared himself to Kopites for his all-action performances, and he further strengthened his bond with supporters by leaping into the Anfield Road Stand to celebrate his equaliser against the LaLiga side six days ago.

His wholehearted and composed displays have already led to some pundits reversing their negative opinions of him when he joined on loan from Barcelona in August, and his reputation as a fans' favourite was embellished by two moments in particular yesterday.

Araujo brilliance summed up by two moments

Liverpool were two goals to the good by the 21st minute on Sunday, but Brighton began to worry the home side towards the end of the first half.

At one point, Maxim De Cuyper attempted to dribble past Araujo when the defender was lying down on the ground, but the Uruguay international nudged the ball away from the Seagulls player with his head whilst on the turf in an attempt to clear the danger.

Then, with 10 minutes of normal time remaining and the visitors applying sustained pressure in the hope of triggering a late comeback, Malick Yalcouye was charging along the left flank until being stopped in his tracks by a thundering challenge from the Reds' number 33, who got to the ball as the Brighton substitute jumped to avoid him.

Araujo's name booming around Anfield after that 81st-minute challenge told you everything about the esteem in which he's already held by Liverpool fans after just 12 appearances for the club.

The Uruguayan feels like a throwback to a different era when defenders were preoccupied by doing their job by any means necessary rather than trying to look neat and tidy, although it'd be disingenuous to label him a mere flat-track bully.

The 27-year-old is also a very good footballer – he wouldn't have played for Barcelona and Liverpool if he weren't – and while other right-backs might have a greater attacking instinct, his presence unquestionably makes the back four stronger.

Araujo was throwing himself into challenges yesterday as though the loss of a clean sheet would be a major personal affront, and the prevailing opinion among many Reds supporters is that the club should waste no time in trying to convert his loan move into a permanent transfer.

If it felt as though there was a disconnect between players and fans towards the end of last season, then the Uruguay colossus has done plenty to re-establish that crucial sense of harmony between those on the pitch and in the stands.
